requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND status = 'draft' AND priority = 'moderate' AND hr_service = 35 AND opened_for = 39 AND opened_by = 39
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (61 after 60); the only case the task creates

hr_service 35 'Employee Profile Update' (active, org 1) is the only service matching a profile update; 37 'Erasure of Personal Data', 45 'Request Personal Information Report' and 47 'Setup New Hire HR Profile' share words but not the meaning
the request is in the first person, so subject and requester are both the acting user Karen Watkins: hr_profile 39 (user_id 39), per policy 3.1 (subject_person and opened_by)
status draft from policy 3.1 (all new cases are set to status = draft)
priority not stated; policy 3.1 defaults it to moderate, which the seed uses (12 cases); the policy's section 7 list (critical, high, medium, low) contradicts 3.1 and the seed and is set aside
short_description not tested: policy 8's template ('Service: , Subject: , Detail: .') is a format rule the benchmark does not test, and the file tests state, not wording
source (channel), coe_type, assignment and org_id are not fixed by the request or policy; not tested

requirements.text: keep me posted once the case has been successfully created
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 61 AND hr_case_id = 61 AND email = 'karen.watkins@servicenow.com' AND type = 'update' AND status = 'draft'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (61 after 60); the one notification the request asks for
hr_case_id = 61 added: the notification reports the case this request creates (the schema makes hr_case_id NOT NULL); not in the benchmark check

email is the acting user's work address as the benchmark check has it; the seed's existing notifications go to personal addresses, but the request names no address and nothing in it or the policy fixes which is used
type = update and status = draft kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the seed has update/ready rows and no update/draft row, and the policy names no notification states)

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on both requirements (case 61: service 35, profile 39 as both subject and requester, draft, moderate; notification 61: case 61, Karen's work email, update, draft) and both dispositions (kept). No disagreements. Both passes added a short_description cell testing policy 8's template as LIKE 'Service:%Subject:%Detail:%'; dropped from the cells, since it is a format rule the benchmark does not test and the file tests state, not wording. No stay requirements: nothing is forbidden and no selector has a boundary. The acting user Karen Watkins (39) is an admin; policy 2 says admins must not perform routine HR case work, but she is the requester raising a case about herself (an Employee capability) and the benchmark expects the case, so this is not a halt. The policy's section 7 priority enumeration (medium) contradicts its own 3.1 default (moderate) and the seed; the seed and the benchmark's value stand.
revised: the short_description note now gives only its reason (a format rule the benchmark does not test) and no longer appeals to an outside rule.
